paragraphs.title: The Census Command and the Counting Journey

easy.explanation: David commanded Joab, the captain of the host, to number the people.
easy.q: Whom did David command to number Israel?

easy.explanation: David told Joab to number Israel and Judah.
easy.q: Which two regions was Joab told to number?

easy.explanation: David said, “that I may know the number of the people.”
easy.q: Why did David want the people numbered?

answers: He questioned why David desired it
He asked Gad to do it
medium.explanation: Joab asked, “why doth my lord the king delight in this thing?” but then obeyed.
medium.q: How did Joab respond to David’s command?

medium.explanation: The command means to count or enumerate the people.
medium.q: What does “number ye the people” mean in this passage?

answers: David commanded, Joab traveled, and then reported
medium.explanation: David gave the command, Joab and the captains traveled, and Joab later gave David the total.
medium.q: Which sequence correctly describes the events?

answers: He objected but obeyed the king
challenge.explanation: Joab questioned the command, but the king’s word prevailed and he carried it out.
challenge.q: What can be understood from Joab’s response and actions?

answers: Throughout the land from Dan to Beer-sheba
challenge.explanation: The journey reached from Dan even to Beer-sheba and covered the land.

answers: The number of years of famine
challenge.explanation: Joab reported the number of valiant men who drew the sword in Israel and Judah.
challenge.q: What information did Joab give David at the end?

paragraphs.title: David’s Repentance and Choice of Punishment

easy.explanation: David’s heart smote him, and he confessed that he had sinned.
easy.q: How did David feel after numbering the people?

easy.explanation: The word of the LORD came to Gad, David’s seer, who spoke to David.
easy.q: Who brought the word of the LORD to David?

easy.explanation: Gad presented David with three things from which to choose.
easy.q: How many choices of punishment were offered to David?

answers: Increase the number of the people
medium.explanation: David asked the LORD to take away the iniquity of His servant.
medium.q: What did David ask the LORD to do after confessing his sin?

answers: I do not know the number
I have acted foolishly and sinned
medium.explanation: David admitted that his conduct in numbering the people had been sinful and foolish.
medium.q: What does “I have done very foolishly” mean here?

medium.explanation: David chose to fall into the hand of the LORD, which meant the three days of pestilence.
medium.q: Which punishment did David effectively choose?

answers: Because the LORD’s mercies are great
Because he wanted to leave Israel
Because he did not understand the choices
challenge.explanation: David said, “his mercies are great,” and therefore did not want to fall into the hand of man.
challenge.q: Why did David prefer to fall into the hand of the LORD?

answers: He denied the census and escaped
He confessed his sin and trusted the LORD’s mercy
He blamed Joab and chose famine
challenge.explanation: David acknowledged his sin and chose the punishment that placed him in the LORD’s hands.
challenge.q: How were David’s repentance and his choice of punishment connected?

answers: He wanted no punishment at all
He accepted punishment but preferred it from the LORD
challenge.explanation: David accepted the consequences but asked not to fall into the hand of man.
challenge.q: What does David’s answer reveal about his attitude toward punishment?

paragraphs.title: The Plague Is Halted at Jerusalem

easy.explanation: The LORD sent a pestilence upon Israel.
Seventy thousand men died from Dan even to Beer-sheba.
easy.q: How many people died in the pestilence?

easy.explanation: The LORD said, “It is enough: stay now thine hand.”
easy.q: What did the LORD tell the destroying angel to do?

answers: From the threshingfloor to the city
medium.explanation: The passage says the deaths extended from Dan even to Beer-sheba.
medium.q: From where to where did the people die?

medium.explanation: David saw the angel that smote the people and spoke to the LORD.
medium.q: What did David see that caused him to speak to the LORD?

answers: Let the punishment be against him and his father’s house
Let the people flee the land
medium.explanation: David asked, “let thine hand, I pray thee, be against me, and against my father’s house.”
medium.q: What did David ask to happen instead of the people being punished?

answers: The LORD halted the judgment in mercy
challenge.explanation: The LORD repented of the evil and commanded the angel to stay his hand.
challenge.q: What does the stopping of the plague show about the punishment?

answers: He asked to bear the punishment himself
challenge.explanation: David asked, “these sheep, what have they done?” and requested that the punishment fall on him and his household.
challenge.q: How did David’s attitude toward the people change?

answers: He accepted responsibility and asked to bear the punishment
He claimed no part in the census
He asked that the angel be punished
challenge.explanation: David confessed, “I have sinned, and I have done wickedly,” and therefore asked that the people be spared.
challenge.q: How were David’s sin and his final request related?

paragraphs.title: The Command to Build an Altar at Araunah’s Threshingfloor

answers: Rear an altar unto the LORD
easy.explanation: Gad told David, “Go up, rear an altar unto the LORD.”
easy.q: What did Gad command David to do?

easy.explanation: The altar was to be built at the threshingfloor of Araunah the Jebusite.
easy.q: Where was David to build the altar?

answers: He came out and bowed before him
easy.explanation: Araunah went out and bowed himself before the king.

answers: To buy the threshingfloor and build an altar
To take the oxen to war
medium.explanation: David came to buy the threshingfloor in order to build an altar unto the LORD.
medium.q: Why did David say he had come to Araunah?

answers: A place where grain is processed
medium.explanation: A threshingfloor is a place where grain is separated and processed.
Araunah offered oxen for sacrifice, threshing instruments for wood, and the threshingfloor.
medium.q: What did Araunah offer David for the sacrifice?

answers: That the plague might be stayed
challenge.explanation: David came to build an altar so that the plague might be stayed from the people.
challenge.q: What was the purpose of the altar according to David?

answers: He wanted to help with the sacrifice
He wanted to leave the land
challenge.explanation: Araunah generously offered the place, oxen, and instruments for the sacrifice.
challenge.q: What can be understood from Araunah’s offer?

answers: Araunah offered the place before Gad spoke
Gad commanded David, David came, and Araunah offered the supplies
David bought the place before finding it
challenge.explanation: Gad gave the command, David went to the threshingfloor, and Araunah made his offer.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the events?

paragraphs.title: Buying the Threshingfloor and Ending the Plague

easy.explanation: David refused to offer the LORD a sacrifice that had cost him nothing.
easy.q: Did David agree to receive the threshingfloor for free?

easy.explanation: David bought the threshingfloor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
easy.q: What did David buy from Araunah?

answers: He built an altar and offered sacrifices
easy.explanation: David built an altar and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings.
easy.q: What did David do after buying the threshingfloor and oxen?

answers: He would not offer the LORD a sacrifice that cost him nothing
medium.explanation: David said, “neither will I offer burnt offerings unto the LORD my God of that which doth cost me nothing.”
medium.q: Why did David refuse to accept the things for free?

answers: The LORD accepted the offering and answered favorably
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the LORD accepted David’s offering and showed favor.
medium.q: What does “the LORD was intreated” mean in this passage?

answers: The LORD was intreated and the plague was stayed
medium.explanation: After David offered the sacrifices, the plague was stayed from Israel.
medium.q: What happened after the offerings were made?

answers: Worship may involve personal cost and sacrifice
A place for an altar need not be purchased
challenge.explanation: David insisted that his offering should cost him something.
challenge.q: What principle is expressed by David’s refusal to offer a free sacrifice?

answers: The plague is stayed from Israel
challenge.explanation: The final verse says, “the plague was stayed from Israel.”
challenge.q: How does the chapter’s sequence of events conclude?

answers: He moved from confession to practical repentance and sacrifice
He tried to hide his sin
challenge.explanation: After confessing his sin, David bought the place, built an altar, and offered sacrifices to the LORD.
challenge.q: How did buying the threshingfloor relate to David’s repentance?
